title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Project Overview
This project analyzed student survey data to better understand how instructor helpfulness may relate to students’ likelihood of participating in a course evaluation survey.
The goal was to practice using R, Quarto, data wrangling, visualization, and interpretation in a marketing research style project.

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Research Question
How does perceived instructor helpfulness relate to students’ likelihood of participating in a survey?
This question connects to marketing analytics because it focuses on understanding audience behavior and what factors may influence participation.

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Why This Matters
Survey participation is important because organizations, schools, and brands often rely on feedback to make better decisions.
If students are more likely to participate when they view instructors as helpful, then communication, trust, and positive experiences may play an important role in response behavior.

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Tools Used

R for data analysis
Quarto for report building
ggplot2 for visualizations
dplyr for data wrangling
haven for reading SPSS data
knitr for clean tables

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Data Wrangling Process
The data first had to be cleaned and prepared before analysis.
Main steps included:

Loading the dataset
Selecting variables related to instructor helpfulness and survey participation
Converting labeled responses into numeric values
Removing missing responses
Grouping responses by helpfulness level
Calculating average participation scores

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Example R Code

library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

rpe_data <- read_sav("RPE - Combined-2019-12-19.sav")

rpe_clean <- rpe_data |>
  mutate(
    R_Helpful_num = as.numeric(as_factor(R_Helpful)),
    RPE_LikelyParti_num = as.numeric(as_factor(RPE_LikelyParti))
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(R_Helpful_num),
    !is.na(RPE_LikelyParti_num)
  )

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Variables Used







Variable
Meaning




R_Helpful
Student rating of instructor helpfulness


RPE_LikelyParti
Student likelihood of participating in the survey


R_Helpful_num
Numeric version of instructor helpfulness


RPE_LikelyParti_num
Numeric version of survey participation likelihood

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Operational Scale
The variables were treated as numeric rating scale variables.
Higher values represented stronger agreement or higher levels of the measured concept.
This made it possible to compare average participation scores across different helpfulness levels.

title: Marketing Analytics
Marketing Analytics
text:
Visualization Code

ggplot(summary_table, aes(
  x = R_Helpful_num,
  y = Average_Participation
)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title = "Instructor Helpfulness and Survey Participation",
    x = "Instructor Helpfulness",
    y = "Average Likelihood to Participate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Main Finding
The analysis showed a positive relationship between instructor helpfulness and students’ likelihood of participating in the survey.
As instructor helpfulness increased, the average likelihood to participate also increased.

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Interpretation
This suggests that students may be more willing to provide feedback when they have a positive experience with the instructor.
For marketing research, this connects to the idea that trust, experience, and perceived value can affect whether people choose to respond or engage.

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Skills Demonstrated
This project demonstrates my ability to:

Work with survey data
Clean and transform variables in R
Use the pipe operator
Create summary tables
Build visualizations with ggplot2
Interpret data findings
Present analysis using Quarto

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Connection to Marketing Analytics
Marketing analytics is not only about sales data. It also includes understanding behavior, attitudes, participation, and engagement.
This project helped me practice using data to explain why people may be more likely to respond, participate, or engage with a survey.

title: Marketing Analytics
text:
Key Takeaway
The RPE project helped me build confidence using R and Quarto to turn raw survey data into a clear research finding.
It shows my ability to combine technical tools with marketing research thinking.

This page highlights my understanding of Google Analytics and how it connects to digital marketing strategy.
Google Analytics helps marketers understand how users find, visit, and interact with websites. It can be used to measure traffic, engagement, conversions, and audience behavior.



Google Analytics is important because it helps marketers make decisions based on data instead of guessing. It can show which pages are getting attention, where visitors are coming from, and what content is helping reach marketing goals.

Learning Google Analytics helps me connect marketing strategy with measurable results. It also shows that I can think beyond creative ideas and understand how performance is tracked.
